law: A cousin tradition to Hupia, stiffened enough by Decay that it moves in hops rather than a walk, kept going the same way on borrowed Blood.
Cousin to Skip, moving a body rather than a moment. D&D class: Ranger, Horizon Walker.
A shape drawn from Steel specifically, never Iron, since the style demands the harder metal. D&D class: Fighter, Samurai.
What Spirit (Martial Spirit) becomes once refined enough to move outside the body entirely. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Astral Self.

The Law of knocking: something struck is pushed back, knocked down, or knocked open. It turns a blow into movement, so a hit under this Law sends a body flying and a knock on a door opens it whether it's locked or not. Guards fear it more for the doors than for the blows. D&D class: Fighter, Battle
The plain, unshaped word for Earth when it's calm — no Lava, no Diamond, nothing beneath the surface stirring. D&D class: Druid, Circle of the Land.
Paired opposite of First, and the harder of the two to claim honestly. D&D class: — an abstract ordinal concept, not a class.

Lava is its own entity, formed when a portion of Fire and a portion of Earth were both siphoned away at once and fused together, rather than being heat that simply leaked from one into the other. D&D class: Druid, Circle of the Land, reflavored to molten/volcanic terrain instead of the standard biom
What a god or Spirit leaves behind besides its Laws — reputation, not power. D&D class: — a narrative concept, not a Law with power.
What a Chronicles entry becomes once enough generations retell it past what actually happened. D&D class: Bard, College of Lore.

Not a summon either — a necromancer's own body and Spirit, deliberately carried into undeath rather than raised from someone else's corpse, which is why it's the only type here that keeps all of its original power instead of a fraction.
The paired opposite of Truth, and the more commonly wielded of the two by a wide margin. D&D class: Bard, College of Whispers.
The practice of pulling someone else's Blood bound Life into your own before it stops moving. D&D class: Warlock, The Hexblade.
A shape that favors reach over spread, the opposite instinct of Ball. D&D class: — a shape modifier, not a class.
A binding Law, gentler than Chain since it holds a thing shut rather than holding it down. D&D class: Wizard, School of Abjuration.
Paired opposite of Shorter, a size modifier applied to almost any shape on this list. D&D class: — a size modifier, not a class.
Another of the Original Sin cluster, Desire stripped of anything but itself. D&D class: Warlock, The Fey.
A pull based Law, gentler than Gravity and choosier about what it actually affects. D&D class: Artificer, Artillerist.
What Mechanical designs suffer without Redundancy or enough Precision behind them. D&D class: — a failure state, not a wielded power.

The opposite of Natural — power shaped by mortal craft like Blacksmith rather than pulled straight from a dying spirit. D&D class: — the concept underlying the Artificer class generally, not a subclass of its own.
A general purpose Law for forcing small changes on something without the full commitment of Transformation. D&D class: Wizard, School of Transmutation.
A narrower cousin of Illusion, hiding only identity rather than the whole truth of a thing. D&D class: Bard, College of Whispers.
A cousin of Blacksmith concerned with moving parts rather than a single fixed shape like Blade. D&D class: Artificer, Artillerist.
A gentler cousin of Fix, closer to Heal than to any Blacksmith repair. D&D class: Cleric, Peace Domain.
The trait category Wisdom and Int both fall under, distinct from anything Martial trains in the body. D&D class: — an ability score category, not a class.

progTitle: the Quiet Shade of Mental State
law: A status rather than a Law, describing whatever a Fear, Confusion, or Sadness splinter has currently done to a mind. D&D class: — a status effect, not a class.
The rarest Law to be wielded in the middle of a War, since almost nothing about combat rewards using it. D&D class: Paladin, Oath of the Ancients.
How quickly a body turns Health into Muscle, Ki, or anything else it needs. D&D class: — a bodily process, not a class.
The raw substance beneath Iron, Steel, and Diamond before any of Gnome's children shaped it further. D&D class: — a raw material, covered by Iron/Steel/Diamond.
A Mechanical law of scale, working at a size too small for Precision alone to manage. D&D class: Artificer, Artillerist.
A Nature adjacent Law, moving a whole group rather than a single Animal. D&D class: Ranger, Beast Master.

What the holy church calls it when Divine or Heal works better than a diluted god's power should allow. D&D class: — not a class in itself, an emergent effect when a Cleric's Divine/Heal power exceeds expectation.
The plainest Law of motion, doing what Flight, Turn, and Speed all do more specifically. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Drunken Master.
Where Gnome's ground never dried after Undine's rain, neither fully Earth nor fully Water. D&D class: Druid, Circle of the Land (wetland).
A Void law of increase, the sibling Add takes when the growth stops being simple. D&D class: — a math modifier, not a class.
Made from a corpse deliberately kept from Decay through Preserve rites rather than left to rot, holding onto noticeably more of the original's power at the cost of speed.
A narrower, more extreme cousin of Micro, rarely wielded outside careful Alchemy work. D&D class: Artificer, Alchemist.

The word for the Spirit Realm's four elements acting together and left alone, without any god shaping them on purpose. D&D class: — the concept underlying the Druid class generally, not a subclass of its own.

It is a type of Magic, scorned by the mass due to it being a bum. D&D class: Wizard, School of Necromancy (official subclass). The Law aimed at cancelling another Law outright, rather than resisting or redirecting it like Resistance does. D&D class: Wizard, School of Abjuration.

The Law of the small cut. Any wound made under it, however shallow, never quite closes on its own. A nick becomes a slow Bleed, and a thousand nicks bring down something no single blow could. It's a duelist's and assassin's Law, useless in one blow and deadly over a long fight. D&D class: Rogue, Swa
What a Dreams vision becomes once something from Hell or the Void gets into it. D&D class: Cleric, Trickery Domain.
Draws from any corpse the way a Zombie does, but only holds its power together after dark, reverting to an inert Corpse the moment the sun rises.

Notus is considered the quiet one who is one that follow Boreas winter rage with a damp autumn. He is one the who stayed net the Sylph dead body still it perished back to another realm far from here. He is one of many deity that control the Season
What happens when Touch is refined the wrong direction, or when Poison gets there first. D&D class: — a status effect, not a class.
A splinter of Love that never lets go, closer kin to Dark than to the Light it started from. D&D class: Warlock, The Fey.
Lava cooled too fast to become Gnome's ground again, left sharp instead of solid. D&D class: Rogue, Assassin.
The Alchemy product Rub is usually applied with, closer to Heal than to any Curse. D&D class: Artificer, Alchemist.
What Age becomes once there's nothing left to trade it for. D&D class: — a natural process, not a class.
Living matter, set apart from Metal and anything Man Made shapes out of it. D&D class: Druid, Circle of the Land.
The Void's word for where any Law first came from, rarely used since most Laws already know their own Origin by name. D&D class: — a meta/definitional concept, not a class.
A temporary, costly Boost that borrows against Fatigue the caster hasn't felt yet. D&D class: Barbarian, Path of the Berserker.

The trade a mortal strikes with a Devil, power lent now against something owed later. D&D class: — this is the mechanic underlying the Warlock class itself, not a subclass of its own. See God Contracts for the ranked contracts gods offer mortals.
A Void law built from a contradiction that refuses to resolve, dangerous to hold for long. D&D class: Bard, College of Lore.
The one sided version of Symbiosis, closer in spirit to Lifesteal than to any fair trade. D&D class: Warlock, The Hexblade.
The face of Time mortals reach for most, since what already happened is the easiest kind of time to touch. D&D class: Bard, College of Lore.
A narrower, gentler version of Tame, binding something small rather than something dangerous. D&D class: Ranger, Beast Master.
An older, clumsier word for what Heal does now, mostly used by those who distrust the holy church's version of it. D&D class: — not distinct enough from Heal to warrant its own subclass.
The broad category Martial, Muscle, and Strength all fall under, as opposed to anything Spirit or Mental. D&D class: — a category, not a class.
A shape built for Earth and Gnome's ground rather than for a fight, favored by those who mine Diamond and Iron out rather than forge them into weapons. D&D class: Artificer, Battle Smith.
One of the four Laws said to walk together at the world's ending, alongside Famine, War, and Apocalypse itself. D&D class: Cleric, Death Domain.
A whole layer of reality built from Dimension, the Void's larger scale version of the same idea. D&D class: Ranger, Horizon Walker.
The wandering Cosmic bodies, grouped together as one Law since none of them alone amounts to much. D&D class: Wizard, School of Divination.

Plasma is the entity born when a sliver of Cosmic was siphoned off as pure velocity alone, nothing else of it carried along — a state too fast for even gods to reckon with. D&D class: Sorcerer, Aberrant Mind (official subclass).
A weaponized sliver of Decay, sped up until years become minutes. D&D class: Artificer, Alchemist.
A narrow Nature Law, moving Life between Flowers rather than between people. D&D class: — too narrow for its own class.
What Aptitude looks like before it's ever been tested against anything. D&D class: — a stat concept, not a class.
A narrow Mechanical law, the difference between a working Blacksmith design and a ruined one. D&D class: Artificer, Artillerist.
The thinnest sliver of Time, gone the instant it's used, which is why almost no one bothers wielding it directly. D&D class: Monk, Way of the Sun Soul.
Another of the Original Sin cluster, close kin to Ego but shared rather than private. D&D class: Fighter, Cavalier.
A shape neutral Law, giving anything — a Dart, a Ball, even a word — the ability to be thrown with force. D&D class: Ranger, Hunter.
The rhythm Blood keeps while Life still holds it, and the first thing Heal checks for. D&D class: — a vital sign, not a wielded power.
Not a Law but a category, covering Elves, Beastman, and every other lineage a mortal can be born into. D&D class: — a category, not a class.
What Anger becomes once a Martial cultivator lets it override Instinct entirely. D&D class: — the mechanic underlying the Barbarian class generally, not a subclass of its own.
A narrower version of Take, holding something rather than keeping it, in trade for whatever a Pacts deal demands back. D&D class: Rogue, Swashbuckler.

The Void's word for everything all its other laws operate on, rarely wielded directly since bending it risks all the rest. D&D class: — foundational and abstract, rarely wielded directly; no class of its own.
The paired opposite of Governance, and the more common of the two throughout most of the Mortal Realm's history. D&D class: Barbarian, Path of the Berserker.
A Void law that sends force back the way it came, cousin to Reflection. D&D class: Fighter, Battle Master.
A minor Void law letting a spell already spent be drawn again, cousin to Reroll but aimed at magic rather than chance. D&D class: Wizard, Chronurgy Magic.
The written form of an Alchemy process, useless without someone who already understands the Law behind it. D&D class: — a document, not a class.
A Mechanical law of building twice so Malfunction in one place doesn't cost the whole design. D&D class: Artificer, Battle Smith.
A Void law that sends anything — force, light, magic — back the way it came, cousin to Rebound. D&D class: Wizard, Bladesinging.
The paired opposite of Bind, and the more dangerous of the two when used on the wrong thing. D&D class: Sorcerer, Wild Magic.
A quiet, defensive Law, keeping something exactly where and how it already is. D&D class: Wizard, School of Abjuration.
A Law that copies an action rather than a shape, distinct from what Clone does. D&D class: Wizard, School of Conjuration.
A Void law that undoes a single outcome and lets Probability decide again. D&D class: Sorcerer, Wild Magic.

The defensive answer to almost anything on this list, weaker the more specific the attack it's built against. D&D class: — the concept underlying damage resistance across several classes, not one subclass.
Bound to a single act of vengeance rather than a necromancer's general command, holding a solid quarter of the original's power but only usable toward that one purpose.
A Void law that runs Time backward over something small, never anything so large it would unmake Causality itself. D&D class: Sorcerer, Clockwork Soul.
The Law that lets the four end times powers move as one instead of arriving as four separate things. D&D class: Ranger, Beast Master.
A shape favored for carrying a Law that needs to stay close to a Person without being wielded outright. D&D class: Wizard, School of Enchantment.
The part of a plant Nature Laws reach first, before Fruit or Flower ever forms. D&D class: — a natural product, not a class.
The Nature side twin of Decay, claiming plants specifically rather than flesh or metal. D&D class: Druid, Circle of Spores.
A minor, contact based Law, most often paired with Ointment rather than used alone. D&D class: — too minor to warrant its own class.
